_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
"The container" is the messages container (".messages-container"), "the button" the scroll-to-bottom button (".scroll-to-bottom-button"), and "the gap" the container's scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop. To "send" a message, fill the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) with it and click the send button ([data-testid="send-button"]). Check every assertion with an eval that has "expect" (or an assert_* or wait_* step): an eval without "expect" asserts nothing. When a step says to record something, do it in one eval without "expect" that stores it in the named window variable, then check that variable. Perform the steps in order. The test seeds a conversation at /c/{{SLUG}} whose first message is "echo message 0". To "open the conversation", navigate to /c/{{SLUG}} and wait for the message input to be visible (allow 30s). To "add message N", send "echo message N" and wait until a [data-testid="message"] element containing the text "echo message N" is visible (allow 30s). While a mouse is pressed on the list, another pointer's release outside it does not end that press. The page provides window.__addCollapsible(): it inserts a 400px block, with a "Collapse" button ([data-testid="collapse-test"]) at its bottom, before the container's bottom sentinel, waits for following to reach it, and resolves to the gap. Clicking the button removes the block.
1. Open the conversation.
2. Enough content that the list actually scrolls: add message 1 and wait until the agent-thinking indicator ([data-testid="agent-thinking"]) is hidden (allow 30s); then add message 2 and wait until the agent-thinking indicator ([data-testid="agent-thinking"]) is hidden (allow 30s); then add message 3 and wait until the agent-thinking indicator ([data-testid="agent-thinking"]) is hidden (allow 30s).
3. Wait until Math.abs(gap) <= 1 is true. The button must not be visible (allow 5s).
4. Eval Math.abs(await window.__addCollapsible()) <= 1 expecting true.
5. In one async eval without expect: dispatch new PointerEvent("pointerdown", {pointerId: 1, pointerType: "mouse", bubbles: true}) on the container; dispatch new PointerEvent("pointerup", {pointerId: 2, pointerType: "touch", bubbles: true}) on document.body; call document.querySelector('[data-testid="collapse-test"]').click(); await two animation frames; store in window.__buttonNow whether the button is visible (it exists, its getBoundingClientRect() has non-zero width and height, and its computed visibility is not "hidden"); then dispatch new PointerEvent("pointerup", {pointerId: 1, pointerType: "mouse", bubbles: true}) on the container.
6. Check that window.__buttonNow is true: the list dropped while the mouse was still pressed on it, so the drop was the reader's.

steps.expression: (() => { const c = document.querySelector('.messages-container'); return Math.abs(c.scrollHeight - c.clientHeight - c.scrollTop) <= 1; })()

(async () => { const container = document.querySelector('.messages-container'); container.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerdown', {pointerId: 1, pointerType: 'mouse', bubbles: true})); document.body.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerup', {pointerId: 2, pointerType: 'touch', bubbles: true})); document.querySelector('[data-testid="collapse-test"]').click(); await new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r))); const btn = document.querySelector('.scroll-to-bottom-button'); const rect = btn ? btn.getBoundingClientRect() : null; const vis = btn ? getComputedStyle(btn).visibility : 'hidden'; window.__buttonNow = !!(btn && rect && rect.width > 0 && rect.height > 0 && vis !== 'hidden'); container.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerup', {pointerId: 1, pointerType: 'mouse', bubbles: true})); })()
